title: One simple setup with reasons: when the reply surprises you
outcomes: Keeps the reason for each setup move when Black answers differently from the model line
Answers an offered pawn by freeing pieces rather than holding the pawn (a rule of thumb)
Chooses a simple developing move over a messy pawn grab
Notices a capture or threat on the board and lets it come before the setup

steps.text: You saw one setup move by move in **A setup is a job for every piece**. Now Black stops following the model. The reasons stay: look for the *job* still open (a pawn in the centre, a piece out, the king safe, the rooks joined) and pick the simplest move that does it. A new black move changes the *move*, not the *reasons*. Start with a reply that wastes time.

A pawn on offer is not a job. **Rule of thumb for club players:** when holding a pawn would cost several moves, free your pieces instead. It is only a rule of thumb. It stops applying when taking the pawn wins material at once and the other side gets nothing back. Two positions follow in which Black offers a pawn. Ask what your pieces want, not what the pawn wants.

**When the setup is the right default, and when it is not.** It is the default while nothing is attacked and an equally good simple move exists (a rule of thumb). It gives way to a capture or a threat on the board. And it fits only positions that look like the setups you know. Next: the same kind of question in three positions. Predict first.

steps.title: Quiet reply, or something to take?
steps.prompt: Black has just replied in each position. In which does a setup move still come first? Predict, then check.
Think of the reply that would bother you most when you play your setup. Write the job that would still be open after it, and the move you would use for that job.
